newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian civil servants strike over cost-cutting.
newsitem.headline: Austrian civil servants strike over cost-cutting.

text.p: Thousands of Austrian civil servants staged a half-day strike on Tuesday in protest against job cuts and a spending freeze by the government.
Some 10,000 finance ministry officials went into work but refused to pick up telephones. The action was supported by customs officials who were not directly involved in the strike.
"The strike is not against the population but a warning to employers," Public Service Union (GOeD) head Siegfried Dohr told state television.
The strike began at midnight and was expected to end at midday on Tuesday. It is the first by public sector workers since a 24-hour protest in 1990.

Austrian civil servants, protected from redundancy by law and relatively well-off in comparison with other public sectors in Europe, have recently become unhappy about government cost-cutting measures.
They say staff numbers have been reduced and pay packets eroded by cuts aimed at ensuring Austria qualifies for a single European currency.
Many civil servants received no pay increase this year as part of the government's austerity drive.

In a season of protests opposition parties are also boycotting parliament until June 10 to try to force an inquiry into the 1989 slaying of Kurdish dissidents in Vienna by suspected Iranian assassins.
